answer.mechanism_primary: PRMT7 is a chromatin-modifying enzyme that deposits repressive arginine methylation at NF-kB target promoters, so removing it de-represses those genes and CD8+ T cells expand.
key_entities: epigenetic repression of NF-kB target promoters

rationale: PRMT7 is known for epigenetic regulation, stress responses and silencing of endogenous retroviral elements, so the natural reading is transcriptional: PRMT7 methylates histones at inflammatory gene loci and keeps NF-kB target genes closed. Deleting or degrading it opens that chromatin, which is why NF-kB target transcripts rise and the CD8+ compartment grows after activation.
